newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money trade strained, rates hold firm.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money trade strained, rates hold firm.

text.p: The Croatian money market trade was strained on Friday with firm rates amid short supply, dealers said.
They foresaw difficulties spilling over into next week.
"Some banks expect large payouts (from their clients' accounts) and higher demand for cash on Saturday, so they withheld offers this morning," one dealer told Reuters.
"The situation is as usual because of weekly tax advances but the monthly pension payment is making things harder," the dealer added.
As many as 17 banks sought some 40 million kuna but only 27.7 million were met by 0900 GMT and lenders only granted call money and short-term funds.

Overall banks' balances sank to a low 405.7 million kuna on Thursday and seven of them bought overnight funds on the money market, mostly to replenish their mandatory reserves though one also had a small shortfall to square.
The banking sector increased its Lombard borrowing from the central bank to 27.4 million kuna this morning after repaying most funds taken earlier this week when liquidity was worst.
Lombard loans are granted at 9.5 percent 12 days a month.
The market call money rates varied around 10.5 percent with smaller deals struck at a higher 11 percent and 9.5 that one foreign bank accepted from a large and sound borrower.
All loans with up to one-week maturity were granted at 11 percent. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
